match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the end-of-period estimate of doubtful debts recorded as an allowance; the returns, bad debts and discounts card only covers actual write-offs, and the government debt card is unrelated.

draft.title: Allowance for doubtful debts
card: Some customers who buy on credit will not pay. At the end of the period, the business estimates how much of its accounts receivable will not be collected.
The estimate is recorded as an expense, called doubtful debts expense. This matches the cost to the period in which the credit sales were made.
The other side of the entry is a credit to the allowance for doubtful debts. This is a contra asset account, which reduces accounts receivable.
On the balance sheet, accounts receivable less the allowance shows the amount the business expects to collect. No named customer's account is changed at this stage.
draft.remember: Estimate bad debts at balance date: expense up, receivables down by the allowance.

a.q: At balance date, Ravi's Hardware in Geelong estimates that $2 000 of its accounts receivable will not be collected. How is this recorded?
opts: Debit expense, credit allowance for doubtful debts
Debit allowance for doubtful debts, credit receivables
a.why: The estimate is an expense, so doubtful debts expense is debited. The credit goes to the allowance, which reduces accounts receivable on the balance sheet. Crediting accounts receivable directly is tempting, but no particular customer's debt has been written off yet.
a.clue: The estimate is an expense, and the credit goes to a contra asset.

b.q: Priya's Cycles in Bendigo has accounts receivable of $30 000. At balance date it records an allowance for doubtful debts of $1 500. What does the balance sheet report for accounts receivable?
opts: $28 500, the amount expected to be collected
$1 500, the amount of the estimated bad debts
b.why: The allowance is deducted from accounts receivable, so the balance sheet shows $30 000 less $1 500, which is $28 500. The $30 000 is tempting because no customer account has been changed, but the allowance still reduces the reported amount.
b.clue: The allowance is a contra asset account.

a.best: Debit expense, credit allowance for doubtful debts

b.best: $28 500, the amount expected to be collected

problems.detail: 'What does the balance sheet report for accounts receivable?' is ambiguous. A VCE balance sheet shows accounts receivable at $30 000, then deducts the allowance to give $28 500 net. A careful student could defend $30 000. Ask for the net amount, or the amount the business expects to collect.

'Receivables down by the allowance' could suggest accounts receivable itself is credited, which question a treats as the wrong entry. 'Estimate bad debts' also uses the next point's term where the card says doubtful debts. Say the allowance reduces net receivables, and no customer account is changed.
The clue 'the credit goes to a contra asset' nearly gives the answer away. Only one option credits the allowance, so a student can match the clue without knowing the entry.

proposal.title: Allowance for doubtful debts
card: Some customers who buy on credit will not pay. At the end of the period, the business estimates how much of its accounts receivable will not be collected.
The estimate is recorded as an expense, called doubtful debts expense. This matches the cost to the period in which the credit sales were made.
The other side of the entry is a credit to the allowance for doubtful debts. This is a contra asset account: it sits against accounts receivable instead of changing it.
The balance sheet shows accounts receivable in full, then deducts the allowance. The result, net accounts receivable, is the amount expected to be collected. No named customer's account is changed.
proposal.remember: Doubtful debts are an expense now. The allowance lowers net receivables, and no customer's account is changed.

a.q: At balance date, Ravi's Hardware in Geelong estimates that $2 000 of its accounts receivable will not be collected. How is this recorded?
opts: Debit doubtful debts expense, credit allowance
Debit doubtful debts expense, credit accounts receivable
Debit accounts receivable, credit doubtful debts expense
a.why: The estimate is an expense, so doubtful debts expense is debited, and the allowance for doubtful debts is credited. Crediting accounts receivable is tempting, but that would change customers' accounts, and no particular customer's debt has been dealt with yet.
a.clue: Has Ravi worked out which customer will not pay?

b.q: Priya's Cycles in Bendigo has accounts receivable of $30 000. At balance date it records an allowance for doubtful debts of $1 500. What net accounts receivable does the balance sheet report?

b.clue: Net means after the contra account is taken off.
